13tplor.Ruel Giganite: Ruel Giganites: huge creatures with misshapen cat-like heads and fanged maws on snake-like bodies as thick as tree trunks, rising from the pits on the plateau when the plague-ridden horde laughs for them (sections 148, 38, 80)
13tplor.Acolyte of Vashna: An Acolyte of Vashna, one of the Darkland remnants sheltering with the Ceners, wearing a Medallion of Protection, fought on the ladder to the platform above the plague laboratory (sections 137, 345)
13tplor.Acolytes of Vashna: Acolytes of Vashna with long-bladed spears on the platform above the plague laboratory, one wearing a Medallion of Protection, while Lone Wolf clings to the ladder below (section 86)
13tplor.Drakkar: A Drakkarim warrior, one of the Darkland remnants in Mogaruith, who runs round a corner straight into Lone Wolf and knocks his weapon away (section 27)
13tplor.Vazhag: Vazhag: the Ceners' rat-men, bred in the spawning vats of Mogaruith, squealing warriors armed with rusty blades, spears and maces
13tplor.Fat Vazhag: A grossly fat Vazhag wrapped in furs, woken on its divan amid a hoard of junk in its burrows under the Skardos Mountains (section 115)
13tplor.Vazhag archer: Vazhag archers, the Ceners' rat-men shooting from the battlements and galleries of Mogaruith
13tplor.Vazhag Lancer: A Vazhag lancer on a captured Slovian horse, skilled with its cavalry lance, charging Lone Wolf as he climbs out of Mogaruith's moat (sections 147, 283)
13tplor.Vazhag pack: A pack of Vazhag answering their Cener master's scream, leaping on Lone Wolf with rusty blades before he can reach the druid (section 90)
13tplor.Vazhag patrol: A patrol of eight Vazhag with swords and maces, led down the steps by a frog-like Tzarg on a chain that sniffs out Lone Wolf's scent (section 262)
13tplor.Pit Agarashi: A Pit Agarashi: a gigantic dog-like beast with a blue-black hide, a crocodile's jaw and fiery red eyes, diseased and scarred, that leaps from its pit and claws up the shaft after Lone Wolf (sections 238, 243)
13tplor.Pit Agarashi (wounded)& Vazhag: The Pit Agarashi, wounded, and Vazhag together
13tplor.Plague Agarashi: A Plague Agarashi: the mummified corpse of a creature in a lidless stone casket, animated by sorcery, that strikes at Lone Wolf's mind and seizes his throat (section 131)
13tplor.Plague Hound: The Plague Hound: a gigantic hound with mad red eyes and foaming yellow fangs that bursts through a doorway, attacking with a psychic blast as well, set on Lone Wolf by its armoured master (sections 221, 325)
13tplor.Defender: The Defender: the armoured warrior who set the Plague Hound on Lone Wolf, charging with his sword raised once the hound falls (section 114)
13tplor.Degradon: The Degradon: a lumbering, diseased beast with a bear-like torso, four taloned tentacles, a bulbous head with huge fishy eyes, a crimson gash of a mouth and a spined tail (sections 120, 186)
13tplor.Exterminus: The Exterminus: a giant bull-like creature with a man's face and fangs that steps out of the tapestry in Arch Druid Cadak's chamber at his command (section 125)
13tplor.Dholdaarg: The Dholdaarg: a great grey lake reptile rearing on a neck as long as a tree, with yellow flaring eyes and jagged black fangs (section 295)
13tplor.Pechdrazil: The Pechdrazil: a spectral creature of shimmering green flame with two whip-like tentacles and a toothless fiery maw, hovering over the stairs by the cave-cells (sections 266, 301)
13tplor.Plaghatar: The Plaghatar: a bog creature whose plant-like tendrils coil round Lone Wolf's legs like vines and drag him into the mire, striking as fast as snakes (sections 19, 47, 339)
13tplor.Stragnah: The Stragnah: a bear-like creature covered in leaves instead of fur, whose thorny creepers drop on Lone Wolf and ensnare him (sections 56, 140, 202, 291)
13tplor.Cener Druid: A Cener Druid, one of the herbalist sorcerers of Ruel, in robes, with a slender rod of power or a dagger, who leads Vazhag through the forest (sections 107, 149, 237, 272)
13tplor.Cener Druid (prone): A fleeing Cener Druid knocked flat into the forest briars by Lone Wolf's power-word, groping for his slender golden rod (sections 144, 185)
13tplor.High Priest: A Cener High Priest, a druid of high rank in a hooded purple cloak with a leather-bound book, who steps through a secret door and turns a dagger into a glowing spike of power (sections 126, 156, 212)
13tplor.Brother Croumah: Brother Croumah, the Cener in charge of the Hall of Sacrifice in Mogaruith, where the dead are raised; he fights with a power rod (sections 122, 290, 316, 54)
13tplor.Ruel War-dogs: Ruel War-dogs: an armoured pack of hunting dogs that bursts into a hall through a hole in its wall just after Lone Wolf fells the guard at the desk (sections 11, 100 and 216)

01fftd.Kraan: A Kraan: the huge black bat-winged flying beast the Darklords' lieutenants ride, with a razor-fanged mouth; fought at 17 and 229, and met in the sky at 34, 29 and elsewhere
01fftd.Vordak: A Vordak: one of the undead, a lieutenant of the Darklords in red robes, who wields a black mace and attacks the mind as well; fought at 29 (on the lake shore), 34 (swooping on a Kraan), 283 and 342 (the hooded stranger on the track)
01fftd.Black Bear: A huge black bear, badly wounded from arrows, that lumbers out from behind a rock, in pain and angry (section 43)
01fftd.Giak: A Giak: a small spiteful Darklord goblin-like soldier, descended from the slaves of Helgedad; here one leaps at the young wizard in the ruins of Raumas and Lone Wolf surprises it (section 55)
01fftd.Madman: A wild old Holmgard citizen who screams that the Kai caused the war and attacks him in the street (section 63)
01fftd.Giak + Doomwolf: A Giak mounted on its Doomwolf, fought as one enemy (sections 72 and 340)
01fftd.Giaks: A band of Giaks with spears, fought as a single enemy (section 208)
01fftd.Winged Serpent: A Winged Serpent that bursts out of a stone statue as Lone Wolf approaches it, immune to Mindblast (section 133)
01fftd.Crypt Spawn: Ten slimy winged creatures hatching out of the skulls in the tomb room, fought as one enemy (section 169). Crypt Spawn are living, not undead, slimy brain-shaped things with black bat wings, suckers and trailing bony limbs, which Darklords summon at will to guard their tombs and chambers (wiki)
01fftd.Burrowcrawler: A Burrowcrawler: a giant slimy grub with long tentacles that drops from a tunnel ceiling to strangle, immune to Mindblast and Animal Kinship (section 170). Burrowcrawlers are six-legged, insect-like Agarashi with a stinger tail, a spiked ridge along the back and a slimy-jawed head, fast diggers (wiki)
01fftd.Leader: The leader of three false soldiers at the footbridge, wearing a Toran garrison tunic, bloodstained bandits who demand Lone Wolf's gear (section 180)
01fftd.Soldier: One of the two men with the false soldier leader, bloodstained bandits met at the footbridge, fought one at a time (section 180)
01fftd.Bodyguard: The scimitar-wielding bodyguard of the merchant's caravan, who confronts Lone Wolf at the tailboard or inside (sections 191 and 220)
01fftd.Marshviper: A Marshviper that wraps round Lone Wolf's leg in the slimy water of a swamp (section 227)
01fftd.Robber: A young swarthy robber with a long curved dagger who attacks from behind the bamboo screen or the counter in the herbalist's shop (sections 231 and 339)
01fftd.Drakkar: A Drakkar: a Darkland warrior, here the hooded ferryman who unmasks in the middle of the lake (section 246)
01fftd.Doomwolf: A Doomwolf: a huge razor-fanged wolf, the mount of the Giaks; four are fought one at a time at 253
01fftd.Gourgaz: A Gourgaz: a large grey, scaly cold-blooded reptile warrior of the Maakenmire swamps who eats human flesh, wielding a black axe, immune to Mindblast; he fells Prince Pelathar and is fought at 255

02fotw.Helghast: A Helghast: a shapeless undead captain of the Darklords, able to take human form, with a skull face, red burning eyes and a black sword. Normal weapons cannot harm it, the Sommerswerd doubles its losses, and it is immune to Mindblast but attacks with Mindforce. Fought in the hold at 17, as a disguised wounded man in the forest at 106 (only the Magic Spear hurts it), on the death-hulk at 237 and at 332. Helghasts are skeletal shape-changers out of Helgedad, rotting-faced with glowing red eyes and usually hooded, used by the Darklords as spies and assassins (wiki)
02fotw.Wounded Helghast: A Helghast already gashed in the chest by Lone Wolf as it bursts into the ship's hold, undead and immune to Mindblast (section 5). Helghasts are skeletal shape-changers out of Helgedad, rotting-faced with glowing red eyes and usually hooded, used by the Darklords as spies and assassins (wiki)
02fotw.Dorier + Ganon: The knight brothers Dorier and Ganon of the Order of the White Mountain, travelling in the coach, who fight as one enemy when attacked (section 7; the same fight at 270, in the other order)
02fotw.Ganon + Dorier: The knight brothers Ganon and Dorier of the Order of the White Mountain, fought as one enemy after the surprise attack at the tavern table (section 270)
02fotw.Zombie Crew: The drowned sailors of a death-hulk, raised as living corpses; they fight as one enemy: four of them at 30 after Lone Wolf crashes through the rotten deck, six at 128. Zombies are corpses animated by magic, usually weak foes, and are used as ship crews (wiki)
02fotw.Giaks: Giaks: the grey-skinned, jagged-sworded foot soldiers of the Darklords, dropped in nets from Zlanbeast onto the Green Sceptre. A crowd on the deck at 146, three in the cabin at 34
02fotw.Halvorc: Halvorc the merchant, one of the coach travellers, beaten and robbed by Lachlan of Ragadorn; with a dagger if he survives the surprise attack (section 60)
02fotw.Zombie Captain: Captain Kelman of the Green Sceptre, sunk in the storm and raised to join the death-hulk fleet as a walking corpse with a dagger, immune to Mindblast (section 66). Zombies are corpses animated by magic, usually weak foes, and are used as ship crews (wiki)
02fotw.Viveka: Viveka, a mercenary adventuress travelling in the coach, with a short sword and fast reactions (section 85)
02fotw.Villager: An angry villager of the cove, among the mob that chases Lone Wolf up the stairs with the Szalls (section 90)
02fotw.Szall: A Szall, one of the small creatures that serve the Darklords, met jumping about a dying man in the forest clearing (section 95), and fighting with the villagers on the stairs (section 90). Szalls are a weak, cowardly but cunning breed of Giak, a failed Helgedad experiment that fled to the Wildlands, a few tolerated by humans in places like Gorn Cove (wiki)
02fotw.Watchtower Guard: A Durenese sentry of the wooden watchtower at the Durenor Forest edge who does not believe Lone Wolf and attacks him with a sword (sections 110 and 157)
02fotw.Street Thief: A street thief of Ragadorn with a long curved dagger, one of three who attack Lone Wolf (sections 131 and 298), fought bare-handed one at a time
02fotw.Street Thief Leader: The leader of the three street thieves of Ragadorn, who demands Lone Wolf's gold with a curved dagger (sections 131 and 298)
02fotw.Priest: Parsion, the priest travelling in the coach, who proves to be the Darklords' assassin and draws a black sword from his robes (section 158)
02fotw.Knight of the White Mountain: A Durenese knight of the Order of the White Mountain who lunges at Lone Wolf's head (section 162)
02fotw.Drakkar: A Drakkar, a black-clad Drakkarim warrior of the Darklords with a broadsword; fought on the Green Sceptre at 326 and 345, and two attack on the death-hulk at 185
02fotw.Trickster: A cheat accused in a tavern who draws a curved dagger and fights to the death in a ring of onlookers (section 241)
02fotw.Harbour Thugs: Three scimitar-armed harbour thugs sent by the false sailor in the tavern, fought as one enemy (sections 268 and 348)
02fotw.Sailor: A grim, brutal sailor who arm-wrestles all comers in the tavern and breaks or kills those who beat him; the contest is fought like combat (section 276)
02fotw.Bridge Guard: A spear-armed soldier guarding a bridge who tries to force Lone Wolf off it; two attack at once (section 282)
02fotw.Town Guard: A town guard of Ragadorn, one of six who attack in the tavern (section 296)
02fotw.Town Guard Sergeant: The sergeant of the six town guards who attack in the tavern, the strongest of them (section 296)
02fotw.Town Guard Corporal: The corporal of the six town guards who attack in the tavern (section 296)
02fotw.Border Guard: A border guard with a spear whom Lone Wolf tries to knock unconscious rather than kill (section 306)

03tcok.Ice Barbarian: A fur-clad warrior of the ice, tall, with slanted eyes and bone weapons, in Vonotar's service; some are possessed with pupil-less white eyes. Met in Ikaya and the ice, fought at 14, 68, 108, 161, 208, 241, 260, 270 and 343 (immune to Mindblast where stated)
03tcok.Kalkoth: A large ice-cave predator that bounds at its prey, jaws open, with a long barbed venomous tongue; hunts alone or in a pack of up to three (sections 32, 123, 138, 147, 180, 259, 263)
03tcok.Baknar: A shaggy white-furred horned ice beast that lopes through the snow and drops on sledges; its stinking oil, when rubbed on the skin, keeps out the cold (sections 78 and 103)
03tcok.Ice Barbarian Mutants: Ice Barbarians mutilated and twisted by Vonotar's necromancy, shuffling out of a hall of vats and corpses, controlled in mind by a head-with-feet creature; fought together as one enemy and immune to Mindblast (section 83)
03tcok.Javek: A two-headed serpent with curved venomous fangs, whose venom is the deadliest natural poison of Magnamund; fought on a ledge over an abyss with the jacket wrapped round the forearm (section 88)
03tcok.Doomwolf: A snarling guard wolf kept by Ice Barbarians and loosed by a lever from a hidden archway, fought one at a time (sections 89 and 343)
03tcok.Helghast: A cloaked undead servant of the Darklords with a Mindblast of its own, vulnerable to the Sommerswerd (sections 99 and 304). Helghasts are skeletal shape-changers out of Helgedad, rotting-faced with glowing red eyes and usually hooded, used by the Darklords as spies and assassins (wiki)
03tcok.Ice Barbarians: Three possessed Ice Barbarians with bone swords toothed along the blade and white pupil-less eyes, fought together as one enemy, immune to Mindblast (sections 106 and 296)
03tcok.Ice Barbarian + Doomwolf: An Ice Barbarian and the last Doomwolf of a sleeping kennel, who attack together and are fought as one enemy (section 137)
03tcok.Ice Barbarian Scout: A large Ice Barbarian on skis with a child in a backpack on his back, a Banach flag flying and a spear levelled; he rushes past after one round of combat (section 158)
03tcok.Akraa'Neonor: Vonotar's huge undead guardian, a green ghoulish monster with a head of tentacles and suckers and one pulsing yellow eye, risen from the moat round the Brumalmarc throne; fought at 164 and 200
03tcok.Akraa’Neonor: Vonotar's huge undead guardian, a green ghoulish monster with a head of tentacles and suckers and one pulsing yellow eye, risen from the moat round the Brumalmarc throne; fought at 164 and 200
03tcok.Crystal Frostwyrm: A scavenging beast with a near-transparent skin showing its pulsing organs and a crystalline head of jagged teeth, living on the remains of those lost in the cavern before Ikaya's stone door (section 265); immune to Mindblast

04tcod.Bandit Warrior: A Vassagonian bandit warrior of Barraka's army, dark-skinned, armed with spear or curved sword; met at the river bank, the mine, the town and the tavern (sections 14, 62, 89, 93, 114, 169, 176, 196, 233, 284, 287, 316)
04tcod.Stoneworm: A huge tunnel-dwelling worm that devours men alive, immune to Mindblast; it chases Lone Wolf's men in the mine tunnel (sections 26, 88). Stoneworms are grey, glistening tunnel-dwelling worms with huge toothy mouths, fast, foul-smelling and leaving a corrosive sticky trail (wiki)
04tcod.Vassagonian Warhound: One of Barraka's armoured war-dogs, red-eyed and fast, loosed at the barricade of Ruanon (section 36). Warhounds are battle-bred dogs, larger and fiercer than ordinary ones, with red-lipped fanged jaws, trainable to one master only if taken from the mother as pups (wiki)
04tcod.Vassagonian Warhounds: Barraka's pack of armoured war-dogs, red-eyed and fast, loosed upon the Sommlending barricade and the plain before Ruanon (sections 193, 260, 277). Warhounds are battle-bred dogs, larger and fiercer than ordinary ones, with red-lipped fanged jaws, trainable to one master only if taken from the mother as pups (wiki)
04tcod.Tunnel Fiend: A warty, glowing, winged, razor-fanged creature that hops through the mine tunnel and leaps at its prey (section 46)
04tcod.Tunnel Fiends: A host of bat-winged scaly reptiles that attack with sharp stalagmite chunks in the mine tunnel after the spore cloud, fought all as one enemy (section 65)
04tcod.Giant Meresquid: A huge tentacled creature of the underground river, greyish-green, that drags rowers from the boat and attacks the crossing (sections 47, 194, 234). The Giant Meresquid is a large grey-green aquatic mollusc with writhing tentacles and green blood (wiki)
04tcod.Wounded Bandit: A bandit with a bloodied, bandaged head who ambushes Lone Wolf in the forest cabin, fighting with his back to the door (section 53)
04tcod.Wounded Guard: A mine tunnel guard already cut in the neck by Lone Wolf's first blow, then fights on with a short sword (section 56)
04tcod.Vassagonian Captain: A mind-skilled Vassagonian warrior in iron and steel who rides the giant Itikar bird; he attacks Lone Wolf on the watchtower roof and drains Endurance unless Mindshield protects, immune to Mindblast (section 77)
04tcod.Bandit Horseman: A Vassagonian cavalryman, first charging with a lance, then fighting on foot with a curved broadsword (section 90)
04tcod.Vassagonian Horseman: A mounted Vassagonian lancer in a plumed helm and crimson breastplate, one of the cavalry charging through the broken barricade (section 333)
04tcod.Vassagonian Warrior: A Vassagonian soldier of Barraka's army, fought at the barricade and in the ruins (sections 153, 186, 310)
04tcod.Tunnel Guard Officer: The plumed, red-sashed leader of the tunnel guards, armed with a halberd; his men stand back so he can fight Lone Wolf alone (section 108)
04tcod.Tunnel Guard Leader: The leader of the guards chasing Lone Wolf through the mine, who fights after the portcullis falls instead of the bridge collapsing (section 125)
04tcod.Tunnel Guard: A guard of Barraka's mine tunnels, fought one at a time (sections 125, 143, 208)
04tcod.Barraka: The Darklord Vashna's champion, a stinking, boot-clad warlord who leads the Vassagonian army and attempts the sacrifice of Madelon at the temple altar in Maakengorge (sections 122, 325). Barraka also enslaved the captured Ruanese for the Maaken mines and wielded the Dagger of Vashna, which Lone Wolf takes when he dies; he was slain in 5054 (wiki)
04tcod.Bandit Patrol: A patrol of three bandits with spears tipped with sticky poison, creeping behind Lone Wolf in the copse near Ruanon (section 133)
04tcod.Drunken Guard: A drunken, bloodshot guard on a ramp, driven to fury when Lone Wolf knocks his companion over the edge (section 138)
04tcod.Bridge Guard: A bored dark-skinned guard in leather armour at the mine's wooden bridge, whittling wood; Lone Wolf surprises him (section 147)
04tcod.Crypt Guards: The two Vassagonian guards of the crypt door in Maaken, who see through Lone Wolf's bluff and fight as one enemy (section 198)
04tcod.Guard: A crossbow-armed guard on the steps who fires a volley and then steps forward to fight (section 285)
04tcod.Guards: Heavily armed swordsmen that rush to meet Lone Wolf at the bridge, fought one at a time (section 202)
04tcod.Bandit Leader: A brute in a brass hauberk with a heavy battle-axe, who leads the bandit assault on the mine entrance and breaks the shield-wall (section 299)
04tcod.Elix: A cat-like creature with green glowing eyes, fanged jaws and hissing, scorching breath, kept behind an iron door (section 308). Elix are lynx-sized, slender, graceful southern cats with sabre-like claws, short tails and green-glowing eyes, and a hiss like escaping steam; partly domesticated, some kept captive here (wiki)

05sots.Palace Gaoler: A Vassagonian guard of the palace dungeons who attacks while Lone Wolf stoops for a sword; the second guard in that fight (section 4, and again at 91)
05sots.Bloodlug: A leech-like salt-water scavenger with a toothed mouth, fast and immune to Mindblast, met in underwater combat (section 12). Bloodlugs are weak but fast salt-water scavengers: jelly-like blobs bristling with short tubes, with a hooked scoop hanging below, jet-propelled by water through those tubes (wiki)
05sots.Horseman: A Vassagonian warrior on horseback who tries to trample Lone Wolf (section 20)
05sots.Vestibule Guard: A trident-armed guard in the palace vestibule, one of a group that includes a blowpipe-firer (section 168)
05sots.Vestibule Guard 2: The second trident-armed guard of the palace vestibule, fought after his comrade falls (section 46)
05sots.Elix: A cat-like creature with glowing green eyes that guards the Imperial Apothecary and its Oede herb (section 57). Elix are lynx-sized, slender, graceful southern cats with sabre-like claws, short tails and green-glowing eyes, and a hiss like escaping steam (wiki)
05sots.Kwaraz: A giant reptile with great curved claws that creeps along walls and ceilings in the sewers, very vulnerable to Mindblast (sections 64 and 110)
05sots.Courier: A Vassagonian courier on horseback whom Lone Wolf drags from the saddle and fights on the ground (section 106)
05sots.Palace Gate Guardians: The pair of guards on the Grand Palace's northern gate, ambushed and fought as one enemy (section 119)
05sots.Sharnazim Underlord: The officer of Maouk's Sharnazim, a bull-necked, flat-nosed warrior with a scimitar and dagger, who breaks into the cellar (section 123). The Sharnazim are elite black-uniformed Vassagonian bodyguards of the Grand Palace and royal family, famed for wide-bladed scimitars called bitikali (wiki)
05sots.Sharnazim Warrior: One of Maouk's Sharnazim, black-robed Vassagonian soldiers, who follows Lone Wolf into the gas-filled tunnel with a herb pad over his face (section 135). The Sharnazim are elite black-uniformed Vassagonian bodyguards of the Grand Palace and royal family, famed for wide-bladed scimitars called bitikali (wiki)
05sots.Armoury Guard: A palace soldier guarding the doors to the armoury, fought when Lone Wolf tumbles down the stairs into his antechamber (sections 159 and 178)
05sots.Steamspiders: A nest of loathsome venomous spiders with skull markings, immune to Mindblast, disturbed in the steaming chimney over the tar-sorkh (section 162). Steamspiders are soft-bellied spiders with bony fangs and sticky black venom that nest together in hot places; acid hurts them (wiki)
05sots.Hammerfist the Armourer: A giant armourer whose right arm is a steel hammer-fist, met in the palace forge room (section 190). He is the armourer of the imperial palace in Barrakeesh, a very broad man whose upper right arm ends in a great steel hammer (wiki)
05sots.Yas: A great constrictor snake that crushes its prey and tries to hypnotize with its red-rimmed eyes (section 194). The Yas is a Vassagonian snake, not poisonous but deadly, with a yellow head, red forked tongue and thick brown blood (wiki)
05sots.Crypt Spawn: Winged, tentacled shadow-horrors conjured by Darklord Haakon from a black mist in his hand, fought in his chamber (section 223). Crypt Spawn are living, not undead, slimy brain-shaped things with black bat wings, suckers and trailing bony limbs, summoned by Darklords at will to guard tombs and chambers (wiki)
05sots.Drakkarim: The Drakkarim, the skull-helmed servants of the Darklords, here a pair who rush into the guard room with black swords (section 231; also 273 and 387). Drakkarim are a human-like race made by Naar, living in nations south of the Darklands and often fighting the northern lands, in the Darklords' service (wiki)
05sots.Itikar: A giant black bird that carries riders, wild unless tamed; Lone Wolf fights one to subdue it and then steals it as a mount (sections 240 and 370). Itikars are giant Vassagonian eagles, black-eyed, razor-taloned and nasty-tempered; years to tame, then loyal, nesting in the Dahir and Vakar Mountains and used as mounts by officers, scouts and couriers (wiki)
05sots.Drakkarim Kraan-rider: A Drakkarim warrior riding a Kraan, a leathery-winged flier, who swoops on Lone Wolf's Itikar over Lake Inrahim with a crossbow and black sword (section 244)
05sots.Dhorgaan: A serpent-like monster conjured by Haakon from mist, with glowing red eyes, weak to an enchanted Jewelled Mace (section 253). The Dhorgaan is a Darklord creation, a glistening serpent-like monster with crimson eyes, an illusion made into a living thing (wiki)
05sots.Drakkar: A Drakkar, the death-masked armoured warrior of the Darklords, met on the Skyrider, the palace and its landing platforms (sections 280, 316, 330, 361, 393)
05sots.Vordak: An undead, skeletal lieutenant of the Darklords in a red robe, immune to Mindblast, who leaps onto Lone Wolf's Itikar from a Kraan (sections 299 and 355)
05sots.Drakkarim Sentry: A Drakkarim sentry at the entrance to the Tomb of the Majhan, taken by surprise (section 324)
05sots.Tower Guards: Two grim Vassagonian guards blocking a tower stair, fought as one enemy (section 334)
05sots.Tower Guard: A Vassagonian guard of the tower bridge, who throws away his crossbow for a steel mace and fights in a frenzy after his brother dies (section 375)
05sots.Darklord Haakon: Darklord Haakon, the Darklord of Kaag who leads the hunt for the Book of the Magnakai, met in the chamber of the tomb with a spiked fist and a fiery blue sceptre-blade (section 353). Haakon is Lord of Aarnak, chief city of the Darklands province Iznogdazokim (wiki)
05sots.Platform Sentry: A sentry with a spear on the Itikar landing platform, met across a wobbling gangplank (section 357)
05sots.Sentry: A spear-armed sentry between Lone Wolf and the Itikar's pen on the landing platform (section 389)

06tkot.Yawshath: A shambling, blunt-nosed, four-clawed monster with glowing eyes that preys on pilgrims in the chapel by the spa of Castle Taunor (sections 12, 155 and 343). Yawshaths are Agarashi, creatures of darkness that hid in mountains and swamps when Naaros fell, and now emerge to terrorise the lands near their lairs (wiki)
06tkot.Altan: Altan, a tall rugged ranger from the northern mountains who carries a longbow of orange toa wood and is the other finalist of the archery tournament, fought as a contest of TARGET points (section 26)
06tkot.Chanda the Taxidermist: Chanda, a taxidermist who ambushes Lone Wolf in his workshop by hurling an acid flask, then fights with a rapier (sections 37 and 208)
06tkot.Thief: A battlefield thief in the hospital tent who is stealing from the wounded and attacks with a curved knife (section 42)
06tkot.Bodyguards: Two hired bodyguards, one wearing a spiked knuckle-duster, ordered to throw Lone Wolf out (section 47)
06tkot.Redbeard: A bearded fighter in a bearskin cloak with a wide-bladed sword, who takes insult at Lone Wolf's words and duels him on horseback (section 71); he later takes Lone Wolf to the Inn of the Crossed Swords (section 256)
06tkot.Pirate Berserkers: Battle-frenzied pirates, immune to Mindblast but not Psi-surge, who board the river boat after a war-horn (section 77)
06tkot.Roark: Roark, the scarred, flamboyant young lordling of Amory who bullies an old man in the tavern and fights with a sword (section 78); he later waits on the road (188)
06tkot.Deldenian River Pirate: A river pirate from Delden, shrieking a battle-cry and swinging a heavy cutlass (section 92)
06tkot.Backstabber: A robber in the dark who threatens and then stabs, here the accomplice who kills his own partner (section 114)
06tkot.Backstabbers: A pair of robbers who attack Lone Wolf with daggers in the street at night, fought as one enemy (section 282)
06tkot.Ravenous Warhound: Goregasher, the Kloon's huge, spiked-collared, slavering hound (section 116). Goregasher is a guard dog kept by the Guild of City Criers in Varetta (wiki)
06tkot.Varetta City Watch: The burly night patrol of Varetta who wait outside the Inn of the Crossed Swords to rob and cart away drunks (section 138)
06tkot.Sewer Door: Not a creature: a door sealed shut with filth, which Lone Wolf must batter open with the combat rules, losing ENDURANCE as fatigue (section 156)
06tkot.Varettian Mercenaries: Three warriors of Varetta in the inn, one scar-faced, who spring up to fight after Lone Wolf offends them (section 159)
06tkot.Armoured Assassin: A hired killer in black steel with a closed helmet, who shoots a crossbow then charges with an axe and shouts abuse; Lone Wolf finds it is a woman (sections 164, 234 and 283)
06tkot.Acolytes of Vashna: A howling mob of Vashna's followers who hack at Lone Wolf's legs while he is on horseback (section 194); probably the red-cloaked procession met at section 151. The Acolytes are a cult devoted to bringing back the fallen Darklord Vashna (wiki)
06tkot.Town Sergeant: A scarred sergeant of a town watch who fights Lone Wolf alone with spear and shield to show off (section 201)
06tkot.River Pirates: Three more river pirates who press forward after the first is killed (section 215)
06tkot.Pirates: Two pirates who attack from behind on the lower deck of the river boat (section 254)
06tkot.Undead Summonation: A score of skeletal hands and the walking dead rising from a frozen graveyard around a church, immune to Psi-surge and Mindblast (section 270)
06tkot.Grave Robbers: A dozen robbers who leap from behind a churchyard wall, led by a decoy wounded man with a rusty scimitar (section 337)
06tkot.Dakomyd: An ancient, long-tailed reptilian guardian of the crypt of the Lorestone, immune to Psi-surge and Mindblast, which crumbles to dust after Lone Wolf takes the stone (sections 344 and 350). Dakomyds can regrow from their dismembered pieces after death, stopped only by an artefact blessed by Kai or Ishir; the base of the skull-like shell is the weak spot, and their larvae look like pale gossamer strands that dissolve intruders with acid (wiki)

07cd.Hound of Death: A huge wolf-like hound, immune to Mindblast but not Psi-surge, that springs out of the gloom of Kazan-Oud and bears Lone Wolf down with claws and burning saliva (sections 8, 78 and 245)
07cd.Dhax: Ghoulish, leathery, webbed-handed creatures with talons and glowing red eyes, who howl and leap out of smoke or stalk closer to pounce; fought as one enemy at sections 19, 249, 253, 299 and 314. Dhax are short, squat, black-scaled, dog-skulled creatures, wolf-and-alligator in look, with webbed taloned digits, cloven hooves, long green tongues and green blood, and they eat their prey alive (wiki)
07cd.Oudakon: A shadowy flame-eyed spirit warrior, living in Kazan-Oud's air, that sweeps out of the Great Hall doorway to hit Lone Wolf with a spiked ball and chain (section 27). An Oudakon is a spectral guardian set by a powerful magician to defend a place, triggered by movement (wiki)
07cd.Zahda Beastmen: Zahda's armoured guards, the Beastmen of Kazan-Oud: long-armed, hairy-handed, taloned, lion-tailed warriors in black armour and skull helms, fought several at once as one enemy (sections 40, 50, 75, 206, 316 and 319). Beastmen are human-beast hybrid mutants, the guards and army of Zahda; commonly boar-snouted and tusked with long clawed arms and tufted tails, in black iron skull helms (wiki)
07cd.Flood of Giant Rats: A seething tide of giant rats that comes up the beach out of the night and must be fought as one enemy (section 45)
07cd.Throne-hall Guard: An armoured crossbow guard in Zahda's throne hall area, met with a fountain and bronze doors behind (sections 62 and 81)
07cd.Lekhor: A venomous, blind-eyed water serpent with long yellow fangs, whose body Lone Wolf is clinging to like a rope after his coracle is smashed (section 76; first seen at 203). The Lekhor is a fanged serpent from Dessi with a red forked tongue and blind white eyes, whose corrosive venom is deadly (wiki)
07cd.Trap-webs: Sticky rope-like cobweb strands in a tunnel stair-chamber that shrink round Lone Wolf and must be fought as an enemy, immune to Mindblast and Psi-surge (section 93)
07cd.Lord Zahda: The white-haired, gaunt, wild-eyed lord of Kazan-Oud, the Darklord-like master of the fortress, who holds the Lorestone of Herdos; fought in the beam of blue light, where Mindblast has no effect on him though Psi-surge does (sections 118 and 202). Zahda is an evil sorcerer who took Kazan-Oud, joining the Lorestone of Herdos's power to a Doomstone from Naaros; the Elder Magi failed to destroy him and instead walled the island in a prison of energy (wiki)
07cd.Flame-man: A burning creature that leaps at Lone Wolf's throat, immune to Mindblast but not Psi-surge, whose burns hurt doubly (section 126)
07cd.Beastman Gaoler: A grim-faced Beastman guarding the cell block stairs, a boar-faced axe-wielding gaoler of Zahda's (sections 142 and 290). Beastmen are human-beast hybrid mutants, the guards and army of Zahda; commonly boar-snouted and tusked with long clawed arms and tufted tails (wiki)
07cd.Lord Zahda (with power-staff): Lord Zahda in the final fight in his hall, striking with a staff that hurls blue fire and ends in a clawed tip; immune to Mindblast and Psi-surge (section 174). Zahda is an evil sorcerer who took Kazan-Oud, joining the Lorestone of Herdos's power to a Doomstone from Naaros (wiki)
07cd.Hactaraton Brood: A mass of young, fanged serpents, each as long as an arm, hatched from eggs in the tunnel; fought as one enemy and venomous (section 178; hatching shown at 63)
07cd.Rahkos: A giant, clawed predatory hand with a jewel in its palm that lives on live human brain; immune to Mindblast but not Psi-surge (sections 198 and 235). The Rahkos looks like a severed human hand with mottled swollen skin, green and black fingers with hooked claws and horned hairy knuckles, and lives only on living human brain (wiki)
07cd.Beastman Gaoler No. 1: The first of two Beastman gaolers who rush in from the cell compound after their comrade falls (section 212). Beastmen are human-beast hybrid mutants, the guards and army of Zahda (wiki)
07cd.Beastman Gaoler No. 2: The second of two Beastman gaolers who rush in from the cell compound after their comrade falls (section 212). Beastmen are human-beast hybrid mutants, the guards and army of Zahda (wiki)
07cd.Tunnel Door: Not a creature: a heavy iron door several inches thick that Lone Wolf must raise to escape, using the combat rules as if unarmed (section 214)
07cd.Giant Hactaraton: A gigantic, green-scaled, one-eyed snake that rises from a rotting nest in the chamber where Lone Wolf wakes, whose bite is venomous (sections 164, 219 and 301)
07cd.Zagothal: A great pale, bloated toad-faced, worm-bodied beast with sores that bask on the beach and strikes with a razor-sharp tongue (section 221). The Zagothal is blind and deaf, so it is easy to evade (wiki)
07cd.Oudagorg: A repulsive giant worm that forces Lone Wolf back up the ramp toward the oval door; especially vulnerable to psychic attack (section 233). The Oudagorg has big inky black eyes it can cover with horny sheaths, short rubbery legs and mandibles, froths purple when it smells food and cocoons it in silk; weak, with a fragile brain (wiki)
07cd.Invisible Whipmaster: A magically hidden enemy whose unseen whip cracks across Lone Wolf, who must be fought without seeing him (section 257)
07cd.Giant Fist: A massive monstrous fist that carries off Tavig down a tunnel and must be struck on the move to break its grip (section 280)
07cd.Vampire Bats: A colony of ravenous, needle-toothed bats with poisonous saliva, nesting on the stairs of the tunnel (section 285; met at 13). Vampire bats here prefer human blood and their saliva is poisonous (wiki)
07cd.Black Lakeweed: A thick mass of coiling lake plants that drags Lone Wolf under the surface of Lake Khor, fought while he is short of air (section 325). Black lakeweed is a grey-green carnivorous plant found in swamps and freshwater lakes across central Magnamund (wiki)

08tjoh.Vordaks: Vordaks: skeletal undead servants of the Darklords, here a gang disguised in robes who pull black-steel maces from their sleeves (sections 8 and 101)
08tjoh.Vordak: A Vordak: a skeletal, black-robed undead creature of the Darklords, clawed and immune to Mindblast; here fought unarmed on the Levitron's deck after the sky-ship attack (section 169; also met at 8, 13, 101 and 287)
08tjoh.Gnaag Helghast: A Helghast: a deadly shape-changing undead servant of Darklord Gnaag, which cannot be killed by an ordinary weapon and shrinks from the Sommerswerd (sections 30, 47, 183 and 308). Helghasts are skeletal shape-changers out of Helgedad, rotting-faced with glowing red eyes and usually hooded, used by the Darklords as spies and assassins (wiki)
08tjoh.Ghagrim: A Ghagrim: a boar-faced, grey-lipped, furry swamp-dweller of the Danarg that licks its rusty iron sword and howls as it attacks (sections 38, 205 and 346). Ghagrim, the man-beasts of the Danarg, were once a gentle primitive folk caring for animals under the Elder Magi, poisoned by the evil of Agarash; thick grey lips, tufted body hair, black eyes, thick necks and yellow boar tusks (wiki)
08tjoh.Bourn the Bowyer: Bourn the Bowyer, the owner of a bow-maker's shop, who shoots at Lone Wolf and then throws his bow and draws a sword (sections 40 and 251). Bourn is a shopkeeper in Tharro with a strong interest in the Silver Bow of Duadon (wiki)
08tjoh.Monks of the Sword: Hostile brown-robed monks of the Sword who cry murder in the alley and draw swords; Paido fights alongside (section 41; also met at 110, 164, 231 and 323)
08tjoh.Taan-spider: A giant, hairy, venomous spider, the Taan-spider, that spins vast rope-like webs in the Danarg swamp and creeps out of the mist (section 52, shown at 278). The Taan-spider has coal-black eyes, venom that forms rope-like webs, and is especially weak to psychic attack (wiki)
08tjoh.Korkuna: A foul shelled creature in a hole whose tendril paralyses Lone Wolf, so it is fought with mind power alone; its shell implodes when it dies (section 74). The Korkuna is an orange-brown, egg-like creature whose gossamer membrane, reflecting light, looks like a pool of water; its tendril injects a nerve toxin, it feeds on blood, and the shell implodes when punctured (wiki)
08tjoh.Drakkarim Horselords: A band of Drakkarim horse-warriors led by a bronze-helmed warlord, who charge into battle on horseback (section 88)
08tjoh.Monks (on horseback): Two mounted monks, the ones who took the heroes' horses, who draw swords and ride at Lone Wolf (section 106)
08tjoh.Silver Swamp Python: A huge silver swamp python with tree-thick coils and venomous fangs that bursts through the creepers of the swamp (section 155, shown at 307). The Silver Swamp Python is a large venomous Danarg snake with massive jaws and double-tiered fangs; a poor attacker but very durable (wiki)
08tjoh.Kezoor: Kezoor: an evil priest and sorcerer who summons spiders and protects himself with spells, immune to Mindblast and Psi-surge; Paido fights beside Lone Wolf (sections 159 and 199). Kezoor is a renegade shaman of Mogaruith and leader of the forbidden sect of Dazudskul, with a bounty from Queen Evaine of Talestria; a tall thin man with hard grey eyes who can revive after death (wiki)
08tjoh.Drakkarim Horselord: The leader of the Drakkarim riders, in a bronze helmet with a visor, who charges after Lone Wolf misses with an arrow (section 162)
08tjoh.Rogue Miner: A scar-faced miner who leaps out of the shadows with a pick-axe handle once the door slams shut (sections 233 and 298)
08tjoh.Hunting Dogs: A pair of hunting dogs that lope in ahead of their masters and must be fought if Lone Wolf is found (sections 241 and 305)
08tjoh.Xlorg: A monstrous clawed, webbed-handed reptile of the Danarg that grabs with sucker-like hands, fought to the death (sections 252, 265 and 313). The Xlorg is a toad-like reptile of the Danarg swamps, about two feet taller than a man, with sharp webbed claws, fond of ambushes (wiki)
08tjoh.Boran: Boran, the black-bearded, one-eyed dwarf innkeeper's son, who attacks across the table, immune to Mindblast but not Psi-surge (section 257)
08tjoh.Anapheg: An Anapheg: a huge pear-shaped beast with a pale hairless body, long forearms, a white lizard head and a spiky furred lower half, which also attacks with mind power; fought on the tree-bridge (section 333, shown at 212). The Anapheg attacks with a Mindblast-like power that lowers Lone Wolf's Combat Skill by 2 without Psi-screen, and is immune to Mindblast itself (wiki)
08tjoh.Rahgu: Rahgu: spindly green creatures that sit on the causeway sniffing marsh gas, hissing and fanged; immune to Mindblast and Psi-surge (section 339)

09tcof.Strongroom Guard: A guard of the strongroom whom Lone Wolf leaps on from hiding; he parries once, then is driven back towards the strongroom (section 3)
09tcof.Zakhan Kimah: The Zakhan, ruler of Vassagonia: a golden-armoured sorcerer-lord, shielded by a web of blue energy and armed with the Orb of Death, who comes to kill Lone Wolf at the West Gate of Tahou (fought at 10, 128 and 188). Kimah led the Sharnazim under Zakhan Moudalla and ruled Ferufezan before taking the throne in 5055 by executing rival princelings; he struck a deal with Haakon to trade Lone Wolf and the Book of the Magnakai for the Orb of Death (wiki)
09tcof.Roctopus: A tentacled cave creature that clings to a wall of the passage and lashes out with long slimy tentacles when woken (sections 32 and 327). The Roctopus is a land octopus with long slimy green tentacles of vice-like grip, nesting in damp places (wiki)
09tcof.Drunken Mercenary: A tavern mercenary, drunk and quick to fight: the comrade of a dagger-wielding soldier, he draws his blade when egged on by the crowd (sections 36, 86 and 260)
09tcof.Drunken Mercenaries: A band of drunken hired soldiers in a tavern, who set on Lone Wolf together (section 119)
09tcof.Crocaryx: The reptilian crocodile-faced guardians of Zaaryx and stewards of the Lorestone, met first with a crystal fire-tube in a corridor (sections 46 and 116). Crocaryx are crocodile-like humanoids from deep in Zaaryx who make a cannon from a crystal tube; Kai kept them alive far past their time to guard the Lorestone, and they died out within a generation after Lone Wolf took it (wiki)
09tcof.Anarian Sky-snake: A winged serpent that preys on travellers on the Anarian plain; fast, with venomous fangs and claws (section 82)
09tcof.Anarian Rangers: Lancers of Tahou in winged helmets, led by a sergeant, who surround Lone Wolf on the plain; he fights the sergeant's six men (section 85)
09tcof.Zaaryx Ghoul: A grey-skinned, man-like ghoul of the buried city of Zaaryx, squatting over a sleeper with a rusty sword (section 97). Zaaryx is the buried city beneath Tahou, built by a race descended from Nyxator, with ziggurats, towers and great black stone stairs; ghouls are undead creatures that feed on warm flesh (wiki)
09tcof.Deldenian Mercenaries: A band of mercenaries from Deldenia, led by a leader who has a debt to settle with Lone Wolf (sections 98, 127 and 308)
09tcof.Ghoul: An undead ghoul with long steel-hard fingers, which drops on Lone Wolf's back from above as he leaves the hollow (section 104). Ghouls are undead creatures that feed on warm flesh (wiki)
09tcof.Ghoul Pack: A pack of unarmed undead ghouls with claw-tipped fingers that swarm into the hollow (sections 254 and 322). Ghouls are undead creatures that feed on warm flesh (wiki)
09tcof.Cave Leekhon: A plated, hulking cave predator with slit-pupilled lidless eyes and a fanged maw, that slinks out of a tunnel to pounce (section 129). The Cave Leekhon is a cave dweller with gnarled armour-like plates over a barrel chest, a ridged forehead, lidless slit-pupilled eyes and a fanged mouth (wiki)
09tcof.6 Doomwolves and Giak Riders: A pack of Doomwolves ridden by Giaks, fought as a single enemy after Lone Wolf is thrown from his horse (section 148)
09tcof.Doomwolf: A huge wolf of the Darklands ridden by a Giak; here a wave of them charge Lone Wolf and Banedon (section 244)
09tcof.Psi-ghoul: A ghoul with a swollen, lopsided skull and venom dripping from its tongue, whose mist-cone fails against Lone Wolf's psychic defence; it attacks with an iron spike (sections 166, 191 and 301). Ghouls are undead creatures that feed on warm flesh (wiki)
09tcof.Senate Guards: Three guards of the Anarian Senate who wait at the foot of the stairs with wooden staves to beat the entangled Lone Wolf (section 182)
09tcof.Zadragon: A huge black-scaled dragon-like monster of the deep that threatens to swallow Lone Wolf whole (sections 214, 277 and 336). The Zadragon is a powerful denizen of Zaaryx, the buried city under Tahou, with a head as broad as a horse's body, glistening black scales and fanged jaws; it can be avoided, and the Psychic Ring lets Mindblast work on it (wiki)
09tcof.Pickpocket: A thief with a stiletto who attacks as Lone Wolf steps into the building (section 217)
09tcof.Drakkarim Assault-troopers: Three red-cloaked Drakkarim, fanatical battle-frenzied warriors who pour through the holed West Gate, fought as one enemy (section 220)
09tcof.Sergeant and Guard: A guard sergeant and one of his men, the first pair of the tower guards to be fought in the narrow corridor (section 238)
09tcof.Tower Guards 3 and 4: A pair of tower guards fought together in a narrow corridor (sections 238 and 309)
09tcof.Tower Guards 5 and 6: The last pair of tower guards, fought together in the corridor (section 238)
09tcof.Tower Guards 1 and 2: The first pair of tower guards, fought together in the corridor (section 309)
09tcof.Tower Guard and Sergeant: The last pair of the tower guards, one guard and their sergeant (section 309)
09tcof.Gourgaz: A large, scaly creature wielding a two-handed axe that leads Giak scalers over the battlements of Tahou (section 249)
09tcof.Giak Scouts: A company of Giak scouts looting a village, grabbed by surprise after their Kraan drops them (section 285)
09tcof.Gatehouse Guards: Two burly guards with swords who burst in on Lone Wolf and Sogh as they flee, fought with Lone Wolf unarmed (section 316)

10tdot.Drakkarim Garrison: Drakkarim troops of Torgar's garrison, rallying with shields in the dingy streets after the gate is breached; fought together with the Palmyrion survivors (sections 2 and 318)
10tdot.Partisan Horseman: A rider of the partisans of the pretender Jarel who bars the escape from the cave camp (sections 23 and 170)
10tdot.Partisan Horsemen: A sergeant and his partisan horsemen, who attack with long straight swords (section 118)
10tdot.Partisans: Five sworn men of the partisan leader's camp, who draw their swords at a cue (sections 132 and 216)
10tdot.Ciquali: Dome-headed, ghoulish swamp dwellers with throat sacs and webbed hands that climb aboard the boat from the river (sections 28 and 245). Ciquali are cunning, vicious Hellswamp amphibians with webbed hands and feet, throat sacs and hairless dome heads, with a taste for human flesh and ritual scars marking warriors (wiki)
10tdot.Halgar: A man in crimson leather with a copper-studded bullwhip and a dagger, met in the charred tower (sections 33 and 208). Halgar is Sebb Jarel's brother, a native of Eru, whose signature weapon is the bullwhip (wiki)
10tdot.Roark: The black-robed leader of a cult who summons the Demonlord Tagazin; he draws a slim sword to defend himself (section 41)
10tdot.Lapillibore: A giant worm-like creature with huge clacking mandibles, that bursts out of a cliff face over the gorge (sections 54 and 304)
10tdot.Bhakish: A bloated, fish-like swamp creature with taloned paws that climbs over the boat (sections 76 and 311). The Bhakish has a fish-like head, scaly taloned forepaws, needle-thin fangs and a bloated body, and screams more than croaks (wiki)
10tdot.Akataz Pack: A pack of Akataz, savage war-dogs, hungry to avenge their dead (section 81). Akataz are fierce wild dogs of the forests of Zaldir and Nyvoz, trained by the Drakkarim as hunters and camp guards, and used in packs against cavalry (wiki)
10tdot.Akataz: A savage Drakkarim war-dog, fought in numbers in the forest; especially vulnerable to psychic attack (sections 77, 81 and 254). Akataz are fierce wild dogs of the forests of Zaldir and Nyvoz, trained by the Drakkarim as hunting dogs and camp guards; they love horsemeat and go for horses first, so packs are used against cavalry (wiki)
10tdot.Élite Death Knights: A squad of elite Drakkarim Death Knights, in thick armour, who guard the doors to the Lorestones (sections 109 and 320). The Death Knights are an elite kind of Drakkarim warrior (wiki)
10tdot.Baron Shinzar (with Ogg-kor-kaggaz): Baron Shinzar, the bald Drakkarim commander in plate armour, wielding the axe Ogg-kor-kaggaz whose blade bursts into scarlet flame (section 113). Shinzar was a swarthy giant with a shiny bald head and short black beard, warlord of the Hammerlands for over 400 years, kept alive by the Ogg-kor-kaggaz, which he stole from the Guild of Thieves in Helgor; in 5060 he burned Luomi and took its Lorestone (wiki)
10tdot.Drakkarim: Drakkarim warriors, the Darkland soldiers, two of whom rush at Lone Wolf with raised axes during the charge on the hill (section 115). Drakkarim are a human-like race made by Naar, living in nations south of the Darklands and often fighting the northern lands, in the Darklords' service (wiki)
10tdot.Krorn: A Krorn: a tall, hairless, ape-like brute with long arms that eats its foes, met in the bushes (sections 119 and 315). Krorn are broad, short-legged brutes with black eyes, hairless skulls and leathery knotted skin, from the Moggador and Akamazim forests, who love eating human flesh (wiki)
10tdot.Krorn Pack: A pack of squat, broad Krorn with arms hanging below their knees and knotted skin, led by Baron Shinzar (section 126). Krorn are from the Moggador and Akamazim forests and love eating human flesh (wiki)
10tdot.Cener Ghosts: Spectral mist-wreathed phantoms that feed on life-force, haunting a burial mound (sections 133 and 168)
10tdot.Ziran: A Ziran, a helmed evil Drakkarim warrior of high rank, who has lost his stave of power and fights with a dagger (section 143)
10tdot.Ziran (with Powerstave): A Ziran, an evil Drakkarim warrior wielding a stave of power forged at Helgedad, who wounds the Prince in the temple ruins (section 252)
10tdot.Death Knight: A Drakkarim Death Knight in heavy armour, battle-frenzied, with a two-handed axe or a spear (sections 148 and 180). The Death Knights are an elite kind of Drakkarim warrior (wiki)
10tdot.Gorodon: A lumbering, horned-snouted marsh reptile that attacks through knee-deep mud (section 172). Gorodon are Agarashi reptilian quadrupeds up to 7 metres long, heavily scaled, with two bull-like horns, a smaller nose horn and glowing green pig-like eyes; graceful for their bulk, fearless, in the Hellswamp alone or in groups of three to five (wiki)
10tdot.Taintor Wolf: A huge wolf-beast with great yellow fangs that attacks Lone Wolf and Jarel (sections 187, 336 and 349). Taintor wolves are a massive breed from the Taintor Forest with yellow fangs, hunting in packs, known for cruelty, speed and cunning (wiki)
10tdot.Taintor Wolf (wounded): A Taintor Wolf hurt by Lone Wolf's blow and still attacking (section 312). Taintor wolves are a massive breed from the Taintor Forest with yellow fangs, hunting in packs (wiki)
10tdot.Hammerlander: A leather-clad warrior of the Hammerlands in battle frenzy who breaks through the shield wall (section 211)
10tdot.Hammerlanders: Axe-armed warriors of the Hammerlands who ambush the retreating Lencians in an alley (section 288)
10tdot.Zagganozod: Swarthy warriors, the Zagganozod, with swords and axes, who charge down the river bank after their archers are shot (sections 251 and 344)
10tdot.Pirsian Swordsman: A swordsman of Pirsia, fought alongside a second one (section 274)
10tdot.Demonlord Tagazin: A Demonlord, a huge sabre-toothed jackal of mist and ice, summoned by Roark's followers in the temple (sections 116 and 286). Tagazin is a sabre-toothed, jackal-like Demonlord with creamy skin and knife-sharp talons, a lieutenant of Agarash and servant of Ixiataaga, Deathlord of Ixia (wiki)
10tdot.Drakkarim Assault-captain: A bloated, hugely muscled Drakkarim officer with a scarred, sneering face and a saw-edged scimitar, met on the stairs in the iron tower (section 348)

11tpot.Agtah: An Agtah: a twisted fusion of man and beast, with cat, boar or ram heads, fangs and tusks, the grey horde of the Chaos-master that attacks the Ookor at the bridge and later assails Lone Wolf at Tolakos. Fought alone at 77, 128, 155, 226 and 319; immune to Mindblast
11tpot.Agtah Pack: A pack of six hideous Agtah that spring on Lone Wolf from behind a boulder in the hills after the bridge battle, dragging him down so that the first two rounds are fought unarmed (section 10)
11tpot.Agtah Packleader: A big Agtah, leader of a pack, that jumps Lone Wolf and throws him into the mud after he has downed another, immune to Mindblast (section 37)
11tpot.Agtah Scouts: Two Agtah scouts whose swift, surprising attack is fought together (section 68)
11tpot.Agtah-hound: A dog-sized Agtah with bear-like paws that leaps at Lone Wolf's arm and bites a wrist, after an Agtah has fallen, hampering long weapons and shields (section 201)
11tpot.Amphibian Agtah: A slimy pack of amphibian chaos-beasts of the Agtah kind that attacks Lone Wolf (section 103)
11tpot.Striped Agtah: An Agtah striped with ochre lines that leaps from the back of an onipa at the chariots, so fast that evasion and the Bow are impossible (section 273)
11tpot.Octagtah: An Octagtah: a bloated, warty, tentacled chaos-horror in heavy armour, lashing with poisonous suckered limbs. Three block the Grand Sepulchre's door (sections 34 and 298)
11tpot.Scarlet Warrior: The scarlet warrior: a quick, cat-like fighter in scarlet silk, silver mail and a dragon-faced helmet who rides a giant black winged bird and seizes the two Lorestones at Tolakos, fought with a curved sword (sections 22, 97, 206 and 274)
11tpot.Khozinda: A Khozinda: a stone-scaled, amber-eyed cave beast with a thick lashing tail and a gurgling croak, fought in a cavern (sections 31, 105 and 199)
11tpot.Shadow Reavers (corporeal): The Shadow Reavers in solid form: dark riders with black hands who brandish crackling lances of blue fire and charge to ride Lone Wolf down (section 41)
11tpot.Shadow Reavers: The Shadow Reavers fought as a psychic duel of will, approaching as shadows, with special rules for the combat skill (section 270)
11tpot.Wounded Yoacor: A Yoacor, a giant with golden flesh, wounded by Lone Wolf's arrow in the chest, maddened and fighting on (section 72)
11tpot.Yoacor: A Yoacor: a stern, golden-skinned giant of the Daziarn, guards and mount-riders of the City of Yanis, who speak mind to mind, fought at 225
11tpot.Villains of Sommerlund: Five notorious Sommerlund criminals in costume, Luvias Kort, Falco, Aieta Nematah, Porgron and Gardor Vezh, who were condemned to the Shadow Gate of Toran and serve Vonotar, fought together as one (section 84)
11tpot.Ookor: An Ookor: a stumpy, ape-like, twittering inhabitant of the Daziarn, with a glass-tipped spear, whose chariot guards escort Lone Wolf; suspicious bands attack at 108, 194, 240 and 256
11tpot.Vonotar the Traitor (with Power Ring): Vonotar the Traitor, Lone Wolf's old enemy, a bloated, spider-like sorcerer who steals the last Lorestone and fights with a Power Ring of cold blue fire at the Shadow Gate, immune to Mindblast and Psi-surge (section 120)
11tpot.Tazgar Worm: A Tazgar Worm: a huge winged worm of silvery glow, with sword-sharp fangs, that swoops down on Lone Wolf in the clearing (sections 127, 220 and 257; shown at 141)
11tpot.Chaos-rats: A swarm of huge, verminous chaos-rats that attacks to strip the flesh from Lone Wolf, immune to Mindblast but not Psi-surge (section 187)
11tpot.Chaos-master: The Chaos-master, a thirty-foot evil god of chaos, naked, with ever-shifting features, wielding a stripped tree as a club; Lone Wolf strikes him from the crypt roof at Tolakos while he stalks Lorkon Ironheart (sections 40, 204 and 341)
11tpot.Giant Guakor Lizard: A starving Giant Guakor Lizard of the Plain of Guakor, with curved yellow fangs and foul breath, weakened and especially prone to psychic attack (section 227)
11tpot.Sandai Temple Guards: Two armour-clad creatures guarding the entrance of the Temple of the Sandai at Haagadar, in rusty helmets with face pads, who draw jagged swords when Lone Wolf's bluff fails (section 259)
11tpot.Haagadar Sewer Snake: A giant sewer snake of Haagadar, a colossal cobra-like serpent with a pear-shaped head and burning yellow eyes in a narrow tunnel (section 327)
11tpot.Zhengha: A Zhengha: a dragon-like flier that breathes black, bile-fuelled fire, the scourge of the Plain of Guakor, fought after its smoke gives cover (sections 202 and 329)

12tmod.Egorgh: An Egorgh: a hulking, hairy, lipless beast with cat-like yellow eyes that leaps and lands with a stone-heavy thud, very vulnerable to psychic attack; met in a cave by night (sections 2, 264 and 307)
12tmod.Drakkarim Marine: A Drakkarim marine: a frenzied Darkland sea-soldier boarding the Intrepid, one with a stiletto dagger and burned face, others with swords and axes (sections 4, 7, 100 and 224)
12tmod.Drakkarim Marine Officer: A Drakkarim marine officer with a scimitar, so tough that an arrow shatters against him (sections 5 and 213)
12tmod.Drakkarim Marines: Several Drakkarim marines that rush in once their officer falls, howling and attacking from every side (sections 148 and 347)
12tmod.Drakkarim Marine Sergeant: The sergeant of the enemy assault team on the Intrepid, a Drakkarim in a studded leather battle-mask with a reddened axe (section 248)
12tmod.Drakkarim Sailor: A Drakkarim sailor of an ironclad armed with a billhook, who attacks after Lone Wolf lands on its deck (sections 16, 58 and 194)
12tmod.Ironclad Bo’sun: The bo'sun of an enemy ironclad, a Drakkarim crewman who scrambles up a ladder swinging a sword at Lone Wolf's legs (section 68)
12tmod.Drakkarim Assault Squad: A Drakkarim assault squad led by an officer, howling with fury and throwing themselves at Lone Wolf (section 39)
12tmod.Drakkarim Escorts: A Drakkar escort of several Darkland soldiers who challenge Lone Wolf in the Black City and attack together (sections 45 and 231)
12tmod.Drakkarim Gunner: A Drakkarim gunner, a Darkland ironclad crewman who tries to cut Lone Wolf down after his captain and mate fall (sections 239 and 259)
12tmod.Drakkarim Gunners: Drakkarim gunners caught by surprise as Lone Wolf leaps in among them (section 292)
12tmod.Drakkar: A Drakkar, a soldier of the Darkland race, such as one with a saw-edged sword that jumps up after being knocked down (sections 175 and 198)
12tmod.Drakkar (surprise attack): A Drakkar who grabs Lone Wolf from behind in a corridor, believing him a fellow marine until he speaks (section 32)
12tmod.Death Knight Sentinel: A Death Knight Sentinel, an elite skull-faced Drakkar guard with a spear, on a parapet of Helgedad (sections 158 and 189)
12tmod.Giaks: Three squat grey Giaks, Gnaag's lesser soldiers, who spot Lone Wolf by infravision and attack him near the cliffs (section 8)
12tmod.Aarnak Giaks: A Giak gate-guard of Aarnak with two subordinates who draw swords on Lone Wolf (section 27)
12tmod.Aarnak Giak Sentry: A Giak sentry of Aarnak, suspicious that Lone Wolf has stolen the Zlanbeast, who draws his short sword (section 108)
12tmod.Giak Sentries: Two Giak sentries who rush along the battlements with spears after the alarm bell is rung (sections 22 and 247)
12tmod.Giak Archers: Four Giaks with loaded bows, caught without their swords to hand (section 161)
12tmod.Giak Wagon-guard: The Giak companion of a wagon driver, who parries Lone Wolf's blow and fights on (section 182)
12tmod.Vladoka: A Vladoka, an elite Nadziranim temple guard in Helgedad whose weapon makes him immune to psychic attack (section 15). Their kind are the Nadziranim sorcerers' picked temple guards (wiki)
12tmod.Vladoka (wounded): A wounded Vladoka, an elite Nadziranim temple guard of Helgedad, fought to the death (section 289)
12tmod.Plaak: A Plaak: a small jelly-like thing with a fanged maw that drops from the ceiling and springs at Lone Wolf's face, immune to psychic attack (sections 23, 136 and 205)
12tmod.Xargath: The Xargath, a legendary giant reptilian sea monster of the Kaltersee with scaly head, hooded green-glowing eyes and razor fangs, that smashes the Intrepid; Lone Wolf leaps astride its neck (sections 35 and 192; sighted at 60)
12tmod.Ictakko: An Ictakko: a screeching winged cave horror that explodes from a chasm, trailing a black tendril that delivers a numbing electric shock (sections 55 and 226)
12tmod.Ictakko (wounded): An Ictakko already wounded in its tendril by an arrow, fought after it dives at Lone Wolf (section 276)
12tmod.Crypt Spawn Flood: A squealing flood of Crypt Spawn, loathsome creatures summoned by Darklord Kraagenskûl, which Lone Wolf holds off with the Sommerswerd (sections 57 and 109)
12tmod.Minions of Taktaal: A group of creatures of Darklord Taktaal who ambush Lone Wolf, mistaking him for a minion of their rival Ghanesh by his robe's colour (sections 67, 83 and 104)
12tmod.Darklord Kraagenskûl (wounded): Darklord Kraagenskûl, Lord of Argazad, a corpse-like Darklord with a snake-like parasite in his jaw, hand severed by the Sommerswerd and still fighting with his black sword (sections 75 and 275)
12tmod.Darklord Kraagenskûl (without Helshezag): Darklord Kraagenskûl fought after Lone Wolf has taken his black sword Helshezag, now cowering and clawing (section 133)
12tmod.Darklord Kraagenskûl: Darklord Kraagenskûl, a skeletal Lord of Argazad, fought with a sword of black fire, here against the Dagger of Vashna (sections 171 and 195)
12tmod.Darklord Gnaag: Darklord Gnaag, the insect-eyed ruler of the Darkland empire, who carries the sword Nadazgada and is fought in Helgedad (section 88)
12tmod.Darklord Taktaal (wounded): Darklord Taktaal, a putrescent Darklord of Helgedad: a smooth, ice-white head with a distending muzzle full of razor-sharp fangs and eyes that burn with black fire, on a fur-covered, serpentine body riddled with disease, his black crystal mace hung from his neck. Met wounded by the Transfusor (section 230)
12tmod.Mind Reaper: A Mind Reaper: a winged spirit-beast with glowing ghost-eyes summoned from the Plane of Darkness by Gnaag, which feeds on fear and is very vulnerable to psychic attack (sections 102 and 114)
12tmod.Ligan: A Ligan: a warty-handed, Nadziranim-kind being whose psychic probe uncovers Lone Wolf's disguise and who stabs with a dagger (sections 160 and 348). The Liganim are the apprentices of the Nadziranim: tall, slow, often hunchbacked, pale-faced with pig-like snouts, hungry for rank and given to treachery (wiki)
12tmod.Helgedad Ghouls: Two Helgedad Ghouls in a tunnel: swollen, stinking corpse-faces with eyes sewn shut, hooked claws, immune to psychic attack (section 170)
12tmod.Sea-scavenger: A Sea-scavenger: a large sea-bird with a dagger-sharp beak that dives at Lone Wolf, its mate killed (sections 268 and 337)
12tmod.Imperial Sector Guards: The guards of the Imperial Sector of Helgedad who detect Lone Wolf with a psychic probe and draw their battle swords (section 291)
12tmod.Xaghash: A Xaghash: a squat, horny-skinned lizard-like creature with milky eyes, wielding a black steel axe, blocking an exit (section 342). The Xaghash are also called lesser Darklords and must feed on warm-blooded prey to keep their strength; not to be confused with the sea monster Xargath (wiki)

14tcok.Drakkarim: Drakkar: the human warriors of the Darklands, the Darklords' armies, met as guards and soldiers in Kaag (fought at 151, 162, 182, 205, 210, 292, 330)
14tcok.Drakkarim Veterans: Two hardened Drakkarim swordsmen escorting a Helghast on the bridge over the flaming moat, who keep advancing after it is blasted into the fire (sections 5, 132, 280)
14tcok.Drakkarim Handlers: Drakkarim keepers of the war-dog pen in Cadak's pens, who rise to attack when the dogs raise the alarm (section 92)
14tcok.Drakkarim Guards: Drakkarim guards of the cell, who rush in with swords drawn after the Doomwolf falls (section 206)
14tcok.Drakkarim Death Knights: Heavily armoured elite Drakkarim in spiked, skull-faced helms, a pair of which stand at the top of the thorny shaft (section 288); others chase Lone Wolf with crossbows in the streets
14tcok.Korozon: A giant octopus-like creature in a pool in a rubble-choked chamber under Kaag, immune to psychic attack (section 14). It can squirt a corrosive venom from a hooked beak, has green eyes and razor-clawed tentacles, and can attack psychically (wiki)
14tcok.Vodok: A taloned, sharp-toothed, iron-shelled beast with scarlet eyes that guards the platform where Banedon lies; its corpse gives off a shadow that is a polymorphed Nadziran (sections 39, 197; then 150)
14tcok.Vordak: An undead skull-headed warrior of the Darklords, fought with an iron mace in the ruined streets (section 118); needs the Sommerswerd's bonuses. Vordaks are grey-skinned, skeletal undead lieutenants of the Darklords, first raised by Vashna in the dungeons of Helgedad; each is formed around a crystal of power and reverts to it when destroyed (wiki)
14tcok.Vordaks: Three skull-headed undead Vordak who attack with combined psychic bolts and heavy iron maces (section 219)
14tcok.Vordak & Giak patrol: A Vordak lieutenant with six Giak soldiers on patrol, who spot Lone Wolf in the ruins by the square (section 129)
14tcok.Xaghash: Scaly, iron-hard reptile brutes with evil eyes, met in pairs, that shrug off arrows; the Sommerswerd doubles its power against them (sections 62, 263). The Xaghash are also called lesser Darklords and must feed on warm-blooded prey to keep their strength (wiki)
14tcok.Ligan: A hunched, hooded, pig-snouted thrall of the Nadziranim, armed with a rod; a Ligan fought here wields the green-glowing Ziranakag rod that turns into a flaming spiked ball (section 72). The Liganim are the apprentices of the Nadziranim, ambitious, insecure and treacherous (wiki)
14tcok.Gnagusk: A shaggy, chained boar-headed beast with great curved tusks, loosed on the drawbridge over the burning moat (sections 89, 102, 122, 221, 299). A Gnagusk is a boar-like Darkspawn creature (wiki)
14tcok.Plaak: Jelly-like discs with two sets of snake fangs dripping venom, hung from a tunnel roof as living assassins of the Nadziranim, immune to psychic attack (section 126). Plaak are grey, disc-shaped jelly creatures that can cling to any hard surface; Nadziranim and Liganim use them as assassins (wiki)
14tcok.Zavaghar: A huge six-legged, mustard-coloured rodent beast with a giant jaw of spade-shaped teeth, kept by Arch Druid Cadak (section 128)
14tcok.Akataz: A Drakkar war-dog, a vicious hound especially open to psychic attack (sections 135 wounded by an arrow, 286 ripping free of a curtain)
14tcok.Nadziran: A Nadziranim sorcerer, master of Right-handed magic, here in dragon guise with a flaming sword and a psychic assault that drains Lone Wolf (sections 169, 211). The Nadziranim are Darklands wizards with an ant-colony mind, utterly obedient; their true form is a semi-transparent, goat-like, ghoulish biped with small horns and claws, and they cannot leave the Darklands in it, so they take lesser shapes such as a fire dragon (wiki)
14tcok.Giant Doomwolf: A huge starving wolf of the Darklands, tethered in a cell, that breaks its rope and leaps at Lone Wolf (section 195)
14tcok.Ashradon: A huge gull-winged, red-skinned reptilian monster with black streaming hair, immune to Mindblast and Psi-surge, that swoops at Lone Wolf as he carries Banedon (section 229)
14tcok.Kaag Kraan: Three flying spawn of Kaag, bat-winged creatures with claw-tipped wings that dive from the smoky sky at Lone Wolf at a street corner (sections 279, 303)
14tcok.Ice Dragon: A frost-white dragon with black eyes and a freezing breath, the final shape of the dark shadow and polymorphed Nadziran (section 281)
14tcok.Egorghs: Three hulking shaggy ape-like beasts that leap at Lone Wolf, especially susceptible to psychic attack (section 318)

15tdc.Ciquali: A scaly, dome-headed amphibian of the Hellswamp with bulging eyes, webbed claws and throat sacs, attacking boats in packs; warriors bear ritual scars (sections 7, 111). The Ciquali are a cunning, flesh-eating breed of Hellswamp amphibian who scar themselves to mark warriors; they also appear in Book 8 (wiki)
15tdc.Ciquali Chieftain: The big Ciquali chief, with bone armour that stops an arrow, who knocks Prarg aside and attacks Lone Wolf (section 228)
15tdc.Death Knight: An armoured elite Drakkarim warrior met in a corridor of Darke (section 113)
15tdc.Death Knights: Armoured elite Drakkarim soldiers who climb the tower stairs to trap Lone Wolf (section 254)
15tdc.Drakkarim Escorts: Two Drakkarim, one carrying a sack, who draw swords and rush when Lone Wolf is seen at the doorway (section 116)
15tdc.Drakkarim Sergeant: A Drakkarim sergeant in a cabin, whom Lone Wolf kills before he can raise the alarm (sections 198, 232)
15tdc.Drakkarim Trench-troopers: Four Drakkarim with spears in a trench over a parapet, fought beside Prarg (section 206)
15tdc.Drakkarim Lancer: A Drakkarim cavalry soldier with a lance, leapt on from above (section 244)
15tdc.Mawtaw: A huge albino, bear-sized, sabre-toothed beast with pink eyes and a stubby tail, hungry in the snow, immune to Mindblast and Psi-surge (sections 121, 297; seen at 20). The Mawtaw is the king of the Tozaz Forest, with strong psychic powers it uses to try to hypnotise its prey (wiki)
15tdc.Tunnel Stalker: A lumbering furry hulk with hungry scarlet eyes, long arms holding flint daggers and a bloated belly dripping saliva, met in the tunnels and on stairs under the city (sections 6, 102, 122, 218, 285, 318, 335)
15tdc.Lencian Crusader: A Lencian knight with a steel mace who takes Lone Wolf for a Stornland turncoat; the fight is to knock him out, not kill him (section 154)
15tdc.Warlord Magnaarn (with Nyras Sceptre): The Drakkarim warlord Magnaarn, near undeath from the Doomstone on his Nyras Sceptre, fought at the top of the Palace Tower in Darke (sections 75, 179)
15tdc.Zagganozod Lancers: Two Drakkarim Zagganozod lancers, mounted cavalry in armour with lances, who attack Lone Wolf at the square (section 248)
15tdc.Zagganozod Captain: The sword-wielding leader of a Drakkarim Zagganozod cavalry troop, killed in the Lencian ambush (section 54)
15tdc.Nad-jaguz: A pack of five vicious war-hogs loosed from the base of a log tower (section 249). A Nad-jaguz is a heavy, tusked, coarse-haired species of war hog (wiki)
15tdc.Wild Akataz Pack: A pack of Drakkarim war-dogs, wild and hungry, especially susceptible to psychic attack, attacking Lone Wolf and Prarg (sections 32, 250)
15tdc.Tukodak Guards: Two of Magnaarn's Tukodak spear-bearing guards on the ramp of the temple tower (sections 57, 268)
15tdc.Tukodak Guardians: Armoured Tukodak warriors of Magnaarn in battle-frenzy, met in threes before the gates of Darke (section 272)
15tdc.Antah Wasps: Fist-sized wasp-like insects living in nests in a shaft in the Temple of Antah, with glowing tails that fire venomous stingers, immune to psychic attack (section 281)
15tdc.Tarhdemon: A Nadziranim sorcerer polymorphed into a six-clawed furry beast with a bulbous head and milky eyes (sections 42, 283). The Tarhdemon is a polymorph form of the Nadziranim, wizards of the Darklands (wiki)
15tdc.Armoury Guards: Drakkarim guarding the armoury building, met when Lone Wolf forces a window (section 305)
15tdc.Gartoth: A frilled tentacled sea creature with a single eye, whose iron-hard tentacles seize Lone Wolf; its eye is its weak spot (section 326). The Gartoth is a huge slug-like amphibian whose rope-like tentacles hang from a sac beneath its single eye (wiki)
15tdc.Gorodons: Three charging horned beasts with blazing eyes, which Animal Control fails to halt, attacking in the shallows (section 44). The Gorodons: long, crocodile-like reptilian Agarashi of the Hellswamp, up to about seven metres, with two bull-like horns and a smaller nose horn, pig-like glowing green eyes; they hunt alone or in groups of three to five (wiki)

16tlov.Vortexi: Vortexi: shrieking phantom-like psychic creatures that ride the storms above the Maakengorge and hunt by sensing minds. Lone Wolf is attacked by them at 36, 103, 118, 142, 206, 284 and 305, and must fight them there. The Vortexi are glowing, wraith-like psychic beings that hunt their prey by the strength of its mind waves (wiki)
16tlov.Vorndarol Jackals: A pack of eight ridge-backed, wild jackals of the Lake Vorndarol hills that hunt for live horsemeat and attack Lone Wolf and his horse (sections 11, 99 and 208)
16tlov.Arch Druid Cadak: Cadak, the Arch Druid and Lone Wolf's old enemy, leader of the acolytes of Vashna, met at the Maakengorge dais and fought there using invisibility; immune to Mindblast and Psi-surge (sections 54, 123, 135, 267)
16tlov.Acolytes of Vashna: The robed human followers of Vashna, gathered by the thousand at the Maakengorge; a mob of them attacks Lone Wolf when he is found out in the crowd (section 130) and again when he comes back through the Shadow Gate (section 345)
16tlov.Acolytes of Vashna (in battle-frenzy): Acolytes of Vashna whipped into a maniacal frenzy, charging Lone Wolf, and weaker in combat than the usual mob (section 140)
16tlov.Cheghath: Cheghath: Shamath's attendants, cloaked figures in the Demoness's cavern, who draw thin steel blades from their robes and have strong psychic defences (sections 97 and 132). The Cheghath are Shamath's dark attendants, creatures of Naar (wiki)
16tlov.Vakovarian Brigand Captain: The leader of a gang of Vakovarian brigands lying in ambush by the trail, fought with his sword as Lone Wolf creeps up behind him (section 14)
16tlov.Zarthyn: A Zarthyn: a big bat-winged beast with fangs and claws that drops on Lone Wolf out of the fog on the Plane of Darkness (sections 152 and 254)
16tlov.Lavas: Lavas: three horny-skinned, golden-winged flying creatures that nest in a pile of obsidian cubes on the Plane of Darkness and flicker in and out of sight; fought at 52 (or avoided at 158). Lavas are servants of the dark god Naar, enslaved on the Plane of Darkness, with plated limbs and bellies, snaky tongues in their beaks, and talons; vulnerable around the eyes (wiki)
16tlov.Durncrag Scavengers: Durncrag Scavengers: vulture-like black birds of prey native to the mountains, diving on Lone Wolf's horse as he crosses the river by ferry (section 180)
16tlov.Demoness Shamath (in the guise of Gnekas: Shamath, the giant Demoness who serves Naar, in her guise as Gnekasha the Worm-thrall: a huge crawling worm, its slimy sides covered in small tendrils, a puckered drooling mouth, and a black infant's face with glowing red eyes (section 242). In her cavern of flame jets by the crystal dais she sets Lone Wolf a riddle, and fights him when he fails it (section 216)
16tlov.Crypt Spawn: Crypt Spawn: a squeaking, writhing cloud of flying horrors that fall from the vaulted cavern ceiling on a helpless, half-sunken Lone Wolf (section 232)
16tlov.Black Corvayl: A Black Corvayl: a huge horned black bear-like beast of the northern mountains, hunted for its pelts, that attacks Lone Wolf and his horse (sections 48, 257, 306 and 336). The Black Corvayl is a gigantic black-furred bear with a single horn on its forehead, living in the mountains around the Darklands; its pelt fetches a high price in the Stornlands and Casiorn (wiki)
16tlov.Vakovarian Brigands: A gang of Vakovarian brigands, bandits from the lawless city of Vakovar who infest the road and the Vorndarol shore, attacking with swords and daggers (sections 39 and 268)
16tlov.Shamath Automatons: Shamath's Automatons: a line of armoured warriors with no eyes and no lips, stiff and machine-like, who guard the crystal dais against Lone Wolf, immune to psychic attack except Kai-blast (section 334)

17tdoi.Ixian Mhagani: Ixian Mhagani: an undead beast of the Ixian mountains, a huge bear-like creature with a domed reptilian head, a long twisted horn and a score of slimy tentacles tipped with venomous claws; lurks in a cave in the pass (sections 89, 110, 275)
17tdoi.Chaos-horde: A horde of Chaos-creatures: bloated corpse-things, humanoid horrors and decayed skeletal warriors that follow Lone Wolf's scent through the swamp and the sunken building's stairs (sections 67, 111, 137, 145, 154)
17tdoi.Chaos Horde: The Chaos-horde: a regiment of bloated corpse-things, humanoid horrors and decaying skeletons that charges Lone Wolf on the stone roof of the sunken building (section 278)
17tdoi.Ziog: A Ziog: a three-eyed, skeletal, long-clawed undead ghoul that leaps at Lone Wolf from a gangplank, immune to most psychic attack (sections 121 and 277). The Ziog is a towering undead minion of Ixiataaga with a skull-shaped head, three milky eyes and a maw of barbed fangs; it carries an icy rod that throws cold fire (wiki)
17tdoi.Ziog (damaged): A Ziog already wounded by Lone Wolf's attack, fought again at section 288
17tdoi.Kajarda: Kajarda: ghostly undead guardians of a sealed archway in a black-floored chamber, lightning-swift, whose bodies crumple to dust when slain; arrows pass straight through them (sections 96, 125, 287). The Kajarda are corpse-green undead sentries of the Crystal Spire of Xaagon, servants of Lord Ixiataaga, armed with barbed tridents (wiki)
17tdoi.3 Kajarda: Three Kajarda fought together: ghostly, corpse-green undead sentries with barbed tridents (wiki), lightning-swift, that rush Lone Wolf in the black-floored chamber before the sealed archway in the Crystal Spire, just after he has come through a shimmering curtain of light; slain, they implode and crumble to dust (sections 96, 125, 287)
17tdoi.Cabalah: A Cabalah: an undead creature in mouldering black robes with burning eye sockets, black claws and corrosive venomous blood; one bursts through the Lencian shield-wall at 264. Cabalah are grisly undead whose wounds ooze a black corrosive venom (wiki)
17tdoi.3 Cabalah: Three Cabalah, undead in black robes, ghastly attackers fought together; weak to the Sommerswerd (sections 35, 130, 167, 281)
17tdoi.Ixian Undead: Ixian Undead: skeletal and skull-faced warriors of Ixia, with rust-dulled blades and burning eyes, who garrison Xaagon and the Crystal Spire and swarm the harbour at Fort Azgad (sections 23, 42, 50, 132, 239, 242, 310)
17tdoi.Demonlord Tagazin: Tagazin, a jackal-like Demonlord of Naar who has passed through the Shadow Gate, a huge horned, three-eyed, clawed demon, fought by Lone Wolf (sections 45, 216, 341)
17tdoi.Demonlord Tagazin (injured): Demonlord Tagazin, the jackal-like demon, weakened by his passage through the void: Lone Wolf, sped up by a Brotherhood spell, overtakes him as he flees, and he turns and springs at Lone Wolf's chest, a short fight of two rounds (sections 53 and 230)
17tdoi.Demonlord Tagazin (with Power Helm): Demonlord Tagazin wearing the Power Helm, a stronger form of the jackal-like Demonlord of Naar (sections 142 and 308)
17tdoi.Ixian Gybia: An Ixian Gybia: a massive, fanged underwater monster of the icy lake, bleeding vile green blood, that attacks Lone Wolf as he swims for the shore (section 21)
